events.title: Nellie Bly Begins Her Race Around the World
events.description: Journalist Nellie Bly of the New York World set out from Hoboken, New Jersey, attempting to circle the globe faster than the fictional Phileas Fogg's 80 days from Jules Verne's novel. She completed the journey in 72 days, 6 hours, and 11 minutes.
events.significance: Her journey set a world record at the time and made her an international celebrity, demonstrating the capabilities of women in journalism and adventure.

events.title: Apollo 12 Launches to the Moon
events.description: NASA launched Apollo 12 from Kennedy Space Center with astronauts Pete Conrad, Richard Gordon, and Alan Bean. The spacecraft was struck by lightning twice shortly after liftoff, but the crew and mission control recovered and continued the mission.
events.significance: Apollo 12 became the second crewed mission to land on the Moon, demonstrating precision landing near the Surveyor 3 probe and expanding lunar scientific exploration.

events.title: Birth of Astrid Lindgren
events.description: Swedish author Astrid Lindgren was born in Vimmerby, Sweden. She went on to write beloved children's books including Pippi Longstocking, Emil of Lönneberga, and The Brothers Lionheart.
events.significance: Lindgren became one of the world's most widely read children's authors, with her books translated into around 100 languages and selling well over 100 million copies.

events.title: Coventry Blitz
events.description: German Luftwaffe bombers carried out a massive night raid on the English city of Coventry during World War II, destroying much of the city center and damaging the medieval St Michael's Cathedral.
events.significance: The raid killed hundreds of civilians and became a symbol of wartime destruction and, later, reconciliation, as the ruined cathedral became a center for peace and forgiveness efforts.

events.title: Birth of Mamie Eisenhower Era Figure: Birth of Mamie? Correction: Death Marker Replaced by Birth of Mamie Doud
events.description: Mamie Doud Eisenhower was born on November 14, 1896, in Boone, Iowa. She later became First Lady of the United States as the wife of President Dwight D. Eisenhower from 1953 to 1961.
events.significance: As First Lady during the 1950s, she was a prominent figure in American public life and a style icon of the era.
